$comment: Copy to quota-config.json and customize. Changes take effect on service restart. THE CONFIG IS KING: the library uses exactly what this file (plus the documented QUOTA_*/AB0T_* env vars) declares — it never invents a tier, a limit, a resource, or a noun in a customer-facing sentence. The vocabulary below is deliberately GENERIC SaaS; replace every resource_key, tier and limit with your own.
$comment_engine_mode: local = your own Redis, this process enforces (the default). byo_redis = the same, stated explicitly. bridge = you run no Redis at all; enforcement is delegated to the hosted quota service over the mesh (zero-infra onboarding). See docs/deployment.md.

storage.$_comment_redis_url: local-dev EXAMPLE value (doc-lint:allow R2) — declare YOUR Redis here or via QUOTA_REDIS_URL; since 0.7 the library never invents an endpoint
storage._comment_redis_cluster_confirmed_disable: D-71: ab0t-quota requires a NON-CLUSTERED Redis (the atomic counter's multi-key Lua scripts CROSSSLOT on a cluster). The topology is machine-checked at startup via `INFO cluster`; a cluster REFUSES to start. Set this to true ONLY if your Redis cannot report its topology (some managed Redis trim INFO / disable CLUSTER) AND you know it is not clustered — an operator assertion on the record. It never overrides a positive cluster_enabled:1.
storage._comment_redis_durability_confirmed: D-72: the COUNTER is the admission gate, not a cache. An `allkeys-*` maxmemory-policy lets Redis EVICT a live gauge — the counter then reads zero for a resource that is still running and the library silently over-admits. The policy is machine-checked at startup via CONFIG GET; an evicting Redis REFUSES to start. Set this to true ONLY if your Redis cannot report its CONFIG (some managed Redis disable it) AND you know it does not evict — an operator assertion on the record. It never overrides an allkeys-* policy the server actually reported.
storage._comment_ddb_pitr_confirmed: D-76: the activation ledger and the billing outbox live in DynamoDB — state the library cannot reconstruct. At startup (and on every reconcile pass, D-75) the table is verified: ACTIVE, every GSI ACTIVE, TTL enabled on the `ttl` attribute the library writes, and PITR enabled. Set this to true ONLY if your control plane cannot report PITR (DynamoDB Local answers UnknownOperationException) AND you know backups are on — an operator assertion on the record.
storage._comment_redis_scripting_confirmed: D-73: set true ONLY when the SCRIPT command itself is unavailable/denied while EVAL works. Never overrides a script the server REJECTED — recognised by the 'compil' substring of the server's error, a disclosed heuristic, not an exact match; an unproven script fails CLOSED at first acquire.
storage._comment_connect_retry_seconds: D-2: boot-retry budget for a DECLARED but unreachable Redis, then a typed refusal (0 = fail immediately). Auth failures never retry; never degrades to in-memory.
storage._comment_auto_create_tables: D-3: table creation is OPT-IN (default false). Pre-create the four tables (`provision --emit terraform`) or set true once; self-created tables are tagged.
storage._comment_keyspace: K-1: counter key shape. Absent/1 = today's v1 keys — an existing consumer changing nothing is unaffected. 2 / dual_write=true drive the v1→v2 migration (docs/keyspace.md).

enforcement.$comment_shadow_mode: true = evaluate and alert, never deny. The safe first week in production: you see exactly who WOULD have been blocked before anyone actually is.

$comment_resources: REQUIRED, and the section that matters most: nothing is enforced for a resource you have not declared here, and every customer-facing sentence is built from these fields. `display_name`, `unit` and `action_hint` are the words YOUR END CUSTOMER reads in a 429 — the library owns the sentence, you own every noun in it. `description` is different: admin-facing prose for dashboards and docs, never shown to the end customer. Pick counter_type by how usage behaves: GAUGE = a live count that goes up and down (things that currently exist); RATE = events inside a rolling window (window_seconds required); ACCUMULATOR = a total that only grows until reset_period (spend, volume).

resources.$comment: GAUGE — tracks a lifecycle: increment on create, decrement on delete.
resources.description: Projects that currently exist in the workspace (admin-facing).
resources.action_hint: Archive a project to free up a slot.

resources.$comment: GAUGE — seats. Declare `unit` in its PLURAL form; the library prints the singular at exactly one ("1 seat", "2 seats").
RATE — rolling window; window_seconds is REQUIRED and the counter self-expires. There is no decrement: events age out.
resources.action_hint: Wait a moment and try again.

resources.$comment: ACCUMULATOR — grows until reset_period (daily|weekly|monthly). `precision` sets decimal places; use it for money and fractional volume.
resources.action_hint: Delete unused files, or wait until next month when your allowance resets.

resources.$comment: ACCUMULATOR — spend. `unit` is printed verbatim, so a currency code stays a currency code.
resources.action_hint: Wait until next month when your spending limit resets.

$comment_resource_bundles: Optional. Generic dispatch layer: name → list of resource_keys consumed when one of these is created. The library has no opinion on what bundles represent — pick whatever names suit your domain (instance types, plan tiers, product variants, anything). Use engine.check_for_bundle / increment_for_bundle / decrement_for_bundle in your routes instead of writing per-shape branching logic.
$comment_tiers: Every limit key MUST be a resource_key declared in `resources[]` above. `sort_order` is what the library climbs to find the next plan up when it writes an upgrade prompt — it never names a tier you did not declare, and when there is no higher tier it says nothing rather than something false. `upgrade_url` is the CTA rendered with that prompt.

tiers.description: For growing teams with production workloads
tiers.$comment_per_user: default_per_user_fraction caps any single user at this fraction of the org limit. Prevents one team member from exhausting the org quota. Applied to GAUGE resources only when no explicit per_user_limit is set on the resource.
tiers.$comment_billing_model: A tier may also carry `billing_model` (capacity_only by default — limits with no money side-effects), `price`, and `credit_grant` (what a signup or an invoice-paid event grants). See BILLING_MODELS_GUIDE.md before enabling any of them: they move money.
tiers.$comment_limits_long_form: A limit is either a plain number or an object carrying the per-resource knobs: `limit`; `warning_threshold`/`critical_threshold` (the utilisation at which the library warns — enforcement AND the wording of the message both read these values); `burst_allowance` (temporary headroom above the limit, reported as overage rather than denied); `per_user_limit` (a hard per-user sub-quota that overrides the fraction above).

tiers.$comment_null_limit: null = unlimited (the resource is not enforced on this tier).

billing_integration.$comment: Maps Stripe price IDs to quota tiers (mesh resolver). Stripe events flow: Stripe Dashboard -> POST /api/webhooks/stripe (lib verifies HMAC against AB0T_QUOTA_STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET) -> forwards to payment-service -> payment-service dispatches subscription/invoice events to lib handlers -> lib resolves price_id to tier_id via THIS mapping -> lib reads tier.credit_grant + applies. Library is the policy authority; payment-service is just Stripe state. See BILLING_INTEGRATION.md.
